elements.id-string-3: \title{On-going improvements in the Virgo strain h(t) reconstruction, online noise subtraction and early-warning pipe in preparation for the O4 run}
elements.id-string-4: \author{Monica Seglar-Arroyo on behalf of the Virgo Collaboration}
elements.id-string-5: \address{Institut de Física d’Altes Energies (IFAE), BIST, Barcelona, Spain}
elements.id-string-6: \maketitle\abstracts{In this contribution, we outline the improvements on the strain h(t) reconstruction in preparation for the observing run O4 of AdvancedVirgo+.
elements.id-string-7: These improvements have the main goal to provide a h(t) with high precision and reduce its uncertainties on this quantity to a few percent.
elements.id-string-8: First, we describe how the reconstruction of the strain signal h(t) is performed in Virgo and its link to the interferometer and its calibration.
elements.id-string-9: We highlight how we plan to monitor the optical response of the interferometer and mirrors.
elements.id-string-10: We will describe how we plan to correct the bias of the reconstructed h(t) strain.
elements.id-string-11: We present the new online linear noise subtraction method, developed to successfully tackle correlated noise witness channels that are also present in h(t).
elements.id-string-12: We provide the status of the low-latency h(t) strain reconstruction, which has the main goal to reduce the latency in pre-merger early warning alerts.}
elements.id-string-13: The reconstruction of the gravitational wave strain h(t) in O4
elements.id-string-14: The AdvancedVirgo+ detector is a double-recycled Michelson interferometer sensible to gravitational waves in the 10$\,$Hz-10$\,$kHz band, which is part of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA network.
elements.id-string-15: Since the discovery of gravitational waves in 2015, 90 compact binary coalescences have been detected~\cite{1}.
elements.id-string-16: Various improvements in the reconstruction of the strain signal h(t) have been foreseen for the next observing run, O4.
elements.id-string-17: The length variations of the arms of the interferometer caused by the passage of a gravitational wave are observed as power variations in the output photodiode signal.
elements.id-string-18: However, the ITF is controlled via control loops to be kept on a working point to optimise the sensitivity, so the control loops dominate the output signals in the 10$\,$Hz -100$\,$Hz band, i.e. part of the GW signal is in the control signals.
elements.id-string-19: The reconstruction of h(t)~\cite{2} consists of the combination of the output signal, control signals and witness channels, with the knowledge on the response of the mirror/marionettes actuators and the knowledge of the mirror and interferometer optical response, to go back to the gravitational wave strain h(t).
elements.id-string-20: The derived frequency-independent uncertainties during O3, in the 20–2000 Hz band, are of 5\% in amplitude, 35 mrad in phase and 10 $\mu$s in timing (with larger uncertainties around 50 Hz).
elements.id-string-21: Optical response adjustment in the low-latency h(t) reconstruction
elements.id-string-22: Linear noise subtraction of correlated noises in the low-latency h(t) reconstruction
